subject: astronomy
title: Solar & Lunar Eclipses: Foundations
welcome_lead: When Sun, Moon and Earth line up just right — eclipses happen.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: difference between solar and lunar eclipses.
final_note: Both kinds of eclipse are just careful shadow play.

concepts.def: When one body's shadow falls on another.
Moon blocks the Sun from view.
Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
Dark area where light is blocked.
Darkest middle part of a shadow.
Lighter outer part of a shadow.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth. Its shadow falls on a small strip of Earth and the Sun is hidden — but only for those inside the shadow.
The Earth passes between the Sun and Moon. Earth's shadow lands on the Moon, which turns red — a 'blood Moon'.
The Moon's orbit is tilted, so usually the shadow misses. Eclipses only happen when the alignment is just right — a few times a year.
